name: DynamiCare Rewards
one_liner: Phone-based recovery program for substance use: remote breath and saliva tests, verified by selfie video, earn cash rewards, with a recovery coach.
best_for: Adults working on stopping alcohol, opioids, stimulants or tobacco who respond to concrete rewards
People in outpatient treatment who want accountability between visits
Pregnant people trying to quit smoking (the use studied in a randomized trial)
not_for: Anyone in crisis or thinking about suicide: call or text 988
Anyone who needs medically supervised withdrawal (detox): get in-person care first
People without a smartphone or who are not comfortable testing on camera
short_description: Contingency management by smartphone: verified remote substance tests earn rewards on a restricted debit card, with recovery coaching.
long_description: DynamiCare Health delivers contingency management, a behavioural treatment for substance use in which people earn rewards for verified abstinence and attendance. Members test with connected breathalysers or saliva tests while recording a selfie video, and earn rewards (the company says up to about $100 a month) on a smart debit card that blocks bars and liquor stores. The program also includes a recovery coach, appointment reminders and self-guided lessons, and lasts up to 12 months. It is paid for by some health plans, employers and treatment programs, or by members themselves. A randomized trial of the DynamiCare app for smoking in pregnancy found higher quit rates with incentives; its smoking-in-pregnancy version received FDA Breakthrough Device designation in 2022, which is not clearance.
patient_summary: You take breath or saliva tests on camera through the DynamiCare app, and negative tests and attended appointments earn money on a debit card that blocks spending at bars and liquor stores. A recovery coach checks in with you, and the app has recovery lessons. Some insurers, employers and treatment programs pay for it; self-pay starts at $20 a week.

pricing.starting_price: Self-pay from $20/week; covered by some insurance plans
pricing.notes: Self-pay programs start at $20 a week, billed monthly, with add-ons extra; the full program runs 12 months. Many members are funded by an insurer, employer or treatment program; DynamiCare will check a plan. Rewards earned by members are separate from the fee.

privacy.notes: Operates under a HIPAA Notice of Privacy Practices that says it never markets or sells your information; the policy does not clearly give a deletion right.

seo.title: DynamiCare: Contingency Management for Addiction Recovery
seo.meta_description: DynamiCare uses contingency management with financial incentives, remote drug testing, and coaching to support substance use recovery. HHS-OIG approved.

faqs.a: DynamiCare is a smartphone-based addiction recovery platform that combines contingency management (financial incentives), remote substance testing with selfie verification, and recovery coaching to support people with substance use disorders.

faqs.q: How does DynamiCare's contingency management work?
faqs.a: Patients perform substance tests through the app using connected breath or saliva tests verified by selfie video. Negative tests earn financial incentives on a smart debit card that blocks purchases at bars, liquor stores, and ATM withdrawals.

Yes, DynamiCare is the only company with a favorable HHS-OIG advisory opinion confirming their contingency management program with up to $599 in incentives will not incur sanctions under the federal Anti-Kickback Statute.

Contingency management uses incentives for recovery and is one of the most effective evidence-based psychosocial treatments for substance use disorders, supported by over 100 RCTs and 9 meta-analyses.

primary_uses: Contingency management for alcohol and drug use
Remote, video-verified breath and saliva testing
Rewards for abstinence and appointment attendance

clinical_trials.study: Smartphone-based financial incentives for smoking in pregnancy (DynamiCare app)

citation.authors: Kurti AN, Nighbor TD, Tang K, et al.
citation.title: Effect of Smartphone-Based Financial Incentives on Peripartum Smoking Among Pregnant Individuals: A Randomized Clinical Trial

clinical_trials.outcome: Higher smoking abstinence with app-delivered incentives than best practice alone.
clinical_trials.study_design: Randomized clinical trial: best-practice care vs best practice plus app-delivered incentives

availability.note: Offered through some insurers, employers and treatment programs, or self-pay.
